entries.desc: Canonical scope contract data represents allowed modifies, allowed creates, allowed tests, protected files, explicit excludes, related docs, and execution-boundary categories as first-class fields consumed by scope checks.

evidence.note: Build passed and scope-contract smoke passed; core types now expose ScopePathClassification/ScopeCheckRow and checkScopeContract consumes classifier data for allowed/protected/excluded rows.

entries.desc: A declared source/docs change is classified through the canonical boundary model and produces stable scope check rows with id, status, source path, blocking flag, and next-action hint.

evidence.note: Smoke asserts stable rows such as scope.out_of_scope:src/other.ts with status/source/blocking/action fields and registered lifecycle/runtime pass rows.

entries.desc: Unknown or malformed path classes fail closed with a structured reason instead of being implicitly allowed.

evidence.note: Smoke covers fail-closed unknown paths including unregistered story evidence, unknown metadata, undeclared source, and fixture paths.

entries.desc: Runtime, lifecycle, generated artifact, external authority, direct story JSON, and fixture exclusions remain represented as data and are not collapsed into prose-only plan text.

evidence.note: Runtime and lifecycle registry categories are first-class classifier rows, while unregistered metadata and fixture paths remain out_of_scope rather than prose-only exceptions.

entries.desc: An undeclared runtime source edit and an arbitrary metadata JSON file under a runtime-like directory both block unless the canonical model explicitly permits them.

evidence.note: Smoke verifies registered lifecycle/runtime artifacts pass and arbitrary metadata/source/fixture paths block when undeclared.

entries.desc: Scope checks, guard sessions, and operator-facing scope messages consume the same classifier/table rather than maintaining duplicate ad hoc rule sets.

evidence.note: scope-contract.ts now imports classifyScopePath from the shared classifier; guard-session core consumes checkScopeContract violations from the same path-level decision path.

entries.desc: Registered current-story lifecycle artifacts and registered runtime artifacts are classified as provenance/runtime paths and do not create product scope violations.
Scope contract checks, guard session checks, phase gates, and scope-contract handler output expose stable row fields for classifier decisions: id, status, detail/source, hint, and blocking flag.
Legacy story-tree paths are treated only through the supported legacy metadata path rules, while obsolete story-dir prefixes such as .koala/story are not accepted as lifecycle artifacts.

Nearby but unregistered files such as story evidence notes, arbitrary nested evidence files, unknown metadata JSON, and arbitrary .koala JSON fall through to normal scope enforcement and block when undeclared.
The classifier does not introduce blanket exemptions for .lattice, .koala, docs, docs/story, or evidence directories; arbitrary sibling files remain blocking.
Lifecycle artifact classification cannot satisfy delivery, summary, review, validation, or DONE gate receipts; those gates still require their own signed or structured evidence.

A valid DEV or REVIEW scope acknowledgement for a necessary late expansion records affected paths/items, explicit reason, actor/session, phase, head hash, material hash when available, and structured audit evidence.

evidence.note: Temp-repo transcript passed: scope_contract_acknowledge output includes assurance=acknowledged-expansion, phase, headHash, materialHash, affectedPaths, and persisted acknowledged expansion metadata.

entries.desc: After a valid acknowledgement, the same acknowledged paths are surfaced as review-visible scope expansion rather than a silent normal pass, and lifecycle progress still depends on reviewer acceptance.

evidence.note: Temp-repo transcript passed: follow-up scope_contract_check returns status=warn and acknowledgedPaths includes src/other.ts, keeping the acknowledged expansion visible instead of a silent pass.

entries.desc: Acknowledgement or repair requests missing a reason, using malformed paths or evidence refs, targeting terminal phases, or violating phase policy are rejected with deterministic repair/fallback guidance.

evidence.note: Negative transcript passed: short reason, unsafe relative path, and TEST-phase acknowledgement attempts are rejected with deterministic CLI/policy guidance.

entries.desc: A broad or plan-invalidating scope change remains blocking and points back to PLAN or reviewer decision instead of being accepted as a local acknowledgement.
The main implementation agent cannot self-sign reviewer-only scope evidence, silently expand the frozen contract, or overwrite authored scope/intent without explicit replace semantics.
Fallback behavior for missing reviewer or unsupported host is visibly lower assurance and never receives the same label or gate meaning as independent reviewer evidence.

evidence.note: prewrite guard smoke passed, and acknowledgement transcript uses the lower-assurance acknowledged-expansion label rather than reviewer/independent-review wording.

entries.desc: Focused regression coverage passes for M1-M3 behavior, including the scope-contract smoke and any required process-fact verifier updates for changed gate/classifier semantics.
Synchronized docs describe the new scope row, classifier, guard, and acknowledgement behavior in the roadmap, lifecycle artifact policy, and scope guard guide.

Documentation and final evidence explicitly preserve the wave 1 boundary by naming later roadmap milestones, Authority/Layer 4/customer key work, production receipt claims, and unrelated renderer/scheduler work as non-goals.
Regression evidence covers both accepted registered lifecycle/runtime artifacts and rejected unknown metadata, undeclared source, direct story JSON, and fixture paths.
No test, verifier, or documentation update proves scope by relying on blanket directory exemptions, docs-only assertions, or lifecycle classification as a substitute for validation/review/DONE gates.
Build, focused smokes, process-fact verifier, and lattice validate remain fresh after the final material diff, so stale or partial evidence cannot satisfy wave 1 completion.
